Thank you for reaching out about your MMS issue. I can help you troubleshoot this problem.

To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth (YYYY-MM-DD format), or
- Your customer ID (if you have it)?

Once I have this information, I can begin assisting you.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know what you need me to do next.

Thank you for providing your information, John. To help you fix the MMS issue, I’ll guide you through a few quick checks and steps on your phone.

First, could you please check if you can send or receive regular text messages (SMS) and if your mobile data is working for other apps (like browsing the web)? This will help us determine if the issue is specific to MMS or related to your overall service or data connection.

Let me know the results, and we’ll proceed from there.
Could you clarify how I should check if my mobile data is working for other apps? Should I try browsing the web or do you want me to check something specific on my phone?

To check if your mobile data is working for other apps, please do the following:

1. Turn off Wi-Fi on your phone, so you are only using mobile data.
2. Open a web browser (like Chrome or Safari) and try to visit any website (for example, www.google.com).
3. See if the page loads successfully.

If the website loads, your mobile data is working. If it doesn’t load, let me know what happens (any error messages or if it just keeps loading).

Once you’ve tried this, please let me know the result so we can continue troubleshooting your MMS issue.

I just checked my phone, and it looks like Airplane Mode is currently turned on, so I don’t have any cellular service right now. Should I turn off Airplane Mode and try again, or do you want me to do something else first?

Yes, please turn off Airplane Mode on your phone. Once Airplane Mode is off, wait a few moments for your phone to reconnect to the cellular network. 

After that, try browsing a website again with Wi-Fi turned off to check if your mobile data is working. Let me know the results, and we’ll continue troubleshooting your MMS issue from there.

I turned off Airplane Mode, and my phone now shows a poor signal with 2G and mobile data enabled. However, when I tried to test my internet connection, it failed and said there’s no connection. What should I do next?

Thank you for the update. Since your phone is showing a poor signal and is connected to a 2G network, this can cause issues with both internet access and MMS messaging, as 2G is generally not suitable for these services.

The next step is to change your network mode preference to allow your phone to connect to faster networks like 4G or 5G, if available. Please go to your phone’s network settings and set the preferred network mode to “4G/5G preferred” (or similar wording, depending on your device).

After you’ve changed the network mode, wait a moment for your phone to reconnect, and then try browsing the web again with Wi-Fi off. Let me know if your signal improves and if you’re able to access the internet.

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

I changed my network mode to “4G/5G preferred,” and now my phone shows an excellent signal with 5G and mobile data enabled. However, when I tried to test my internet connection again, it still failed and said there’s no connection. What should I try next?

Thank you for updating your network mode and letting me know the results. Since you now have an excellent 5G signal and mobile data enabled, but still cannot access the internet, the next step is to check your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings. Incorrect APN settings can prevent mobile data and MMS from working.

Please check your APN settings on your phone and let me know if anything looks incorrect or if you see any error messages. If you’re unsure how to check, I can guide you through the process or recommend resetting your APN settings to default.

Would you like instructions on how to check or reset your APN settings?

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I checked my APN settings, and the APN name is set to "internet" with the MMSC URL as "http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc." There aren’t any error messages showing. Do these settings look correct, or should I try resetting them to default?

Thank you for providing your APN details. Since there are no error messages and the MMSC URL appears to be set, the settings might be correct. However, sometimes issues can still occur if the APN settings are not fully aligned with your carrier’s defaults.

To rule out any hidden configuration issues, I recommend resetting your APN settings to default. After resetting, you’ll need to reboot your device for the changes to take effect.

Would you like instructions on how to reset your APN settings and reboot your device, or do you already know how to do this?

APN settings will reset at reboot.
